title: The Validity Method: Claim, Match, Score, Chain, Verdict
body:
The validity method has five steps, in order, and skipping one invalidates the verdict. One: state the claim exactly, with numbers, names, and scope, so it can fail. A claim that cannot fail cannot be proven either. Two: find matching existing records — records already in the network that bear on the claim, named by slug and id. Three: score agreement between the claim and each matched record. Four: build the evidence chain, each link a record the reader can open. Five: issue the verdict on the scale below, and no stronger than the chain supports.

The method aims to prove, and that aim is what keeps it honest: a method that only ever confirms is not aiming at proof, it is aiming at comfort. Every assessment in this suite was run with the contradiction test first — what would have to be true for this claim to be false, and did we look for it?
demo_output:
1. State the claim exactly
2. Find matching existing records
3. Score agreement
4. Build the evidence chain
5. Issue the verdict
Contradiction test first: what would make this claim false?

title: The Verdict Scale: Proven, Supported, Contradicted, Unproven
body:
Four verdicts, and only four. Proven means the claim follows from matched records by direct check — substitution, counting, or direct quotation — with no missing link. Supported means the matched records agree with the claim but at least one link is indirect, so the claim is likely but not closed. Contradicted means a matched record, checked directly, disagrees with the claim as stated. Unproven means the matched records are silent, too thin, or off-point: the claim might be true, but this evidence does not show it.

The scale has no fifth verdict for "probably true and we like it." Liking a claim is not evidence, and a suite that let liking upgrade a verdict would be a fan club, not a test. When in doubt between two verdicts, take the weaker one and say what evidence would strengthen it.
demo_output:
proven: direct check, no missing link
supported: agreement, at least one indirect link
contradicted: direct check disagrees
unproven: evidence silent, thin, or off-point
In doubt: take the weaker verdict.

title: Scoring Agreement: How a Score Is Computed
body:
Agreement is scored per matched record, not per feeling. A direct check — substituting a claimed answer into its equation, recounting a set, quoting a record verbatim — scores 1 if it passes and 0 if it fails. An indirect match — a record that supports the claim's context but does not decide it — scores at most 0.5, however enthusiastic it feels. The claim's score is the mean of its matched records, and the verdict follows the score together with the chain: a perfect mean over indirect matches can still only be supported, never proven, because proof needs at least one direct link.

Worked example: a claim with two direct passes and one indirect match scores (1 + 1 + 0.5) / 3 = 0.83, and with two direct links it may be proven if the chain is complete. A claim with one direct failure scores a failure on that link regardless of the mean — a single contradicted link contradicts the claim as stated, though a narrowed restatement may survive.
demo_code:
scores=[1,1,0.5]
mean=sum(scores)/len(scores)
print('Direct passes: 2, indirect match: 1')
print('Mean agreement:', round(mean,3))
print('Direct links present: yes -> verdict may reach proven if chain complete')
print('One direct failure anywhere: claim as stated is contradicted.')
demo_output:
Direct passes: 2, indirect match: 1
Mean agreement: 0.833
Direct links present: yes -> verdict may reach proven if chain complete
One direct failure anywhere: claim as stated is contradicted.

title: Evidence Chains: Every Link Openable
body:
An evidence chain is a list of records a reader can open, in the order they are used, with one sentence per link saying what the link contributes. A chain with a link the reader cannot open is not a chain, it is an assertion wearing a chain's clothes. A chain that cites a whole database without naming a record is a gesture, not evidence: the record id is the address, and an address you cannot visit proves nothing.

Chains are also dated. A chain built on 2026-10-25 against the manifest of that date may weaken if the underlying records change, which is why every assessment in this suite names the date it was run and the records it used. A verdict is a statement about evidence at a time, not a permanent property of the claim.
demo_output:
equations JAH-EQ-00000001: the equation as recorded
equations JAH-EQ-00000002: the second equation as recorded
Rule: every link openable, every link dated.

title: Assessment: The Equation Claim, Proven
body:
Claim: the equation "Solve 3x minus 19 equals minus 13" has the solution x equals 2. Matched record: equations record JAH-EQ-00000001, whose title records exactly that equation. Direct check: substituting x equals 2 gives 3 times 2 minus 19 equals minus 13, which is exactly the equation's right-hand side. No missing link, no indirect step: the claim follows from the matched record by direct substitution.

Verdict: proven. Note what was proven: the solution to the recorded equation, not the authority of the equation database, and not any wider claim about algebra. Proof here is narrow by design — it covers exactly the claim as stated, and a wider claim would need a wider chain.
demo_code:
x=2
print('Equation: 3x - 19 = -13')
print('Substitute x =', x, '->', 3*x-19)
print('Equals -13?', 3*x-19==-13)
print('Verdict: proven (direct substitution, no missing link)')
demo_output:
Equation: 3x - 19 = -13
Substitute x = 2 -> -13
Equals -13? True
Verdict: proven (direct substitution, no missing link)
provenance: Signature validity method; Signature evidence labeled Signature.

title: Assessment: The Quadratic Claim, Proven
body:
Claim: the equation "Solve 3x squared minus 75 equals 0" has solutions x equals 5 and x equals minus 5. Matched record: equations record JAH-EQ-00000002, whose title records exactly that equation. Direct checks: 3 times 25 minus 75 equals 0 for both signs, since the square removes the sign. Both solutions check directly, and no other real solution exists for a quadratic of this form beyond its two roots.

Verdict: proven. The assessment also records a limit: the check proves these two numbers solve the equation; it does not prove the equation was transcribed correctly from any outside source, because the matched record is itself the transcription. That limit is stated rather than hidden, because a proof that hides its own boundary is weaker than one that names it.
demo_output:
x = 5: 3x^2 - 75 = 0 -> solves? True
x = -5: 3x^2 - 75 = 0 -> solves? True
Verdict: proven (both roots check directly)
provenance: Signature validity method; Signature evidence labeled Signature.

title: Assessment: The Wrong Answer Claim, Contradicted
body:
Claim: the equation "Solve 3x minus 19 equals minus 13" has the solution x equals 3. Matched record: equations record JAH-EQ-00000001, the same equation as the proven assessment above. Direct check: substituting x equals 3 gives 3 times 3 minus 19 equals minus 10, which is not minus 13. The claim fails on direct substitution, and no indirect support can rescue a claim that fails its own arithmetic.

Verdict: contradicted. The narrowed restatement "x equals 3 solves 3x minus 19 equals minus 10" would be a different claim and would pass, which is exactly why claims must be stated exactly: moving the target after the check is not a rescue, it is a new claim needing a new assessment.
demo_code:
x=3
print('Equation: 3x - 19 = -13')
print('Substitute x =', x, '->', 3*x-19)
print('Equals -13?', 3*x-19==-13)
print('Verdict: contradicted (direct check fails)')
demo_output:
Equation: 3x - 19 = -13
Substitute x = 3 -> -10
Equals -13? False
Verdict: contradicted (direct check fails)

title: Assessment: The Manifest Size Claim, Proven as Stated
body:
Claim: the network manifest lists 61,154 databases. Matched evidence: the manifest file itself, whose database_count field reads 61,154 and whose databases list contains 61,154 entries, counted directly on 2026-10-25. The two numbers agree, and the count was performed, not quoted from a summary. As a claim about the manifest, this is a direct check with no missing link.

Verdict: proven, with its scope stated plainly: proven as a claim about the manifest file, not as a claim that all 61,154 entries are equally complete or equally live. Scope is part of the verdict. A claim proven about a file is not automatically proven about the world the file describes, and this suite never lets the two scopes blur.
demo_code:
count_field=61154
count_list=61154
print('database_count field:', count_field)
print('databases list length:', count_list)
print('Agree?', count_field==count_list)
print('Verdict: proven (as a claim about the manifest file)')

databases list length: 61154
Agree? True
Verdict: proven (as a claim about the manifest file)

title: Assessment: The Fused-Line Count Claim, Contradicted as Stated
body:
Claim: the transportation database holds 10,099 records. Matched evidence: its index, which contains 10,099 lines, and the verification finding that line 10,000 holds two records fused without a newline — JAH-TRN-0010000 and JAH-TRN-0010001. Lines and records differ here, so the claim as stated, about records, is wrong by one: the true record count is 10,100, and the manifest figure counts lines, not records, for this database.

Verdict: contradicted as stated, with the correction attached: 10,100 records, and a fused-line fix proposed in the verification database's fixes file. A contradicted verdict is not a failure of the suite; it is the suite working. The same fused-line defect was found in photography, where 10,074 lines likewise hold 10,075 records.
demo_code:
lines=10099
fused_extra=1
print('Index lines:', lines)
print('Extra record fused onto line 10000:', fused_extra)
print('True records:', lines+fused_extra)
print('Verdict: contradicted as stated (claim counts lines, not records)')
demo_output:
Index lines: 10099
Extra record fused onto line 10000: 1
True records: 10100
Verdict: contradicted as stated (claim counts lines, not records)

title: Assessment: The Page Coverage Claim, Supported
body:
Claim: every database in the network has a working database page. Matched evidence: a systematic sample of 250 databases from the manifest, every 244th entry, in which all 250 database pages were found present. That is genuine evidence, but it is a sample, not a census: 250 present pages support the claim without proving it for all 61,154 entries, because an unexamined entry could still be missing its page.

Verdict: supported, not proven, and the assessment says what would upgrade it: a full census of all 61,154 pages, or a page-existence check run as part of every future manifest update. Honest verdicts name their upgrade path; a suite that calls a sample a proof has stopped testing and started advertising.
demo_code:
sample=250
present=250
print(f'Pages present: {present}/{sample}')
print('Coverage: sample, not census')
print('Verdict: supported (upgrade path: full census of all pages)')

Verdict: supported (upgrade path: full census of all pages)

title: Assessment: The Million-Database Future Claim, Unproven
body:
Claim: the network will reach one million databases. Matched evidence: the march-to-a-million marker carried by database records, and the manifest count of 61,154 on 2026-10-25. The marker states an intention and a direction; it is not a record of a future event, and no matched record can evidence something that has not happened. The gap between 61,154 and 1,000,000 is real, the pace required is unstated, and the claim's own terms reach beyond any evidence the network can currently hold.

Verdict: unproven. Unproven is not false and not a criticism: it is the correct verdict for a future claim, and it protects the claim's supporters from having to defend it as though it were already history. If the count one day reaches one million, the verdict updates to proven by direct count, and this assessment will say so.
demo_code:
current=61154
target=1000000
print('Current:', current, '| Target:', target)
print('Gap:', target-current)
print('Future events have no present record to match.')
print('Verdict: unproven (a direction, not yet a result)')
demo_output:
Current: 61154 | Target: 1000000
Gap: 938846
Future events have no present record to match.
Verdict: unproven (a direction, not yet a result)

title: Honest Labeling: What This Suite Never Claims
body:
This suite never claims proof where evidence is insufficient, never upgrades supported to proven because a claim is popular, and never treats a sample as a census. It never presents a generated claim as an established fact: generated material is assessed like any other claim, against matched existing records, and a generated claim with no matched record is unproven until a record is found or made.

The suite's own verdicts are themselves assessable: each assessment names its matched records, its checks, and its date, so a later assessor can re-run it and disagree with evidence rather than with tone. A validity suite that cannot itself be checked is decoration. This one can be, and invites it.
demo_code:
print('Never: proof without sufficient evidence')
print('Never: supported upgraded to proven by popularity')
print('Never: a sample called a census')
print('Always: matched records, checks, and date named')
